spec.description: Animals on the move, analysed as movement: lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge (INBO), jaguars across the Neotropics (Jaguar Movement Database) and sharks, tunas, whales, seals and turtles of the Pacific (TOPP, Animal Telemetry Network). Steps, speeds, turning angles, daily rhythms and distance from home, cross-filtered in the browser with Chaski and Mosaic, on animated trails.

options.content:
### About the data
Three open datasets of animals tracked by GPS or satellite, each read where it is published, through the stack's gateway, which keeps a copy for a month: none of them changes. DuckDB on the server reads each one once per visit and hands the browser a thinned copy; [Chaski](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/chaski) runs every query on the page there.

| Tab | Dataset | Publisher | Licence | Here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gulls | [LBBG_ADULT – Lesser black-backed gulls breeding in Belgium](https://zenodo.org/records/22083084) (2022–2025) | INBO, Research Institute for Nature and Forest; Movebank study, Zenodo | CC0 1.0 | One position per bird every two hours; kilometres from every fix |
| Jaguars | [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.2dh0223), Morato et al. 2018, *Ecology* 99: 1691 | 20 research projects; Dryad, Zenodo copy | CC0 1.0 | One position per jaguar every two hours |
| Ocean | [IOOS ATN Trackline Database, Stanford Block Lab](https://atn.ioos.us/erddap/tabledap/stanford_import_ssm_public.html) (TOPP, 2002–2018) | Animal Telemetry Network, NOAA IOOS, on ERDDAP | Free use and redistribution, not for legal use | Tracks smoothed by a state-space model; one position per animal and day |

**Distances** are straight lines between fixes on a sphere, so they are a floor on what an animal travelled; fewer fixes, a lower floor. **The gulls' colony** is the median of all their positions in June. **Ocean longitudes** past 100°E are moved 360° west, so tracks across the date line draw as one line on a Pacific map.

**Not here:** the jaguars' sex, age and weight ship in the same archive as a spreadsheet misnamed `.csv`, which the reader cannot open from inside the ZIP. Movebank, the largest store of animal tracks, needs an account to download, so only studies also published on Zenodo or Dryad can join.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per bird under every filter, the farthest travellers first, under a row
-- for all of them, whose click lets the birds followed go.
WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM $gullSteps WHERE $__crossfilter($gullFilters)),
c AS (SELECT bird, avg(latitude) AS clat, avg(longitude) AS clon FROM f GROUP BY bird),
b AS (
  SELECT bird, max(colony_km) AS far, min(latitude) AS south, sum(km) AS km, count(*) AS positions,
         sqrt(avg(pow((longitude - clon) * 111.32 * cos(radians(clat)), 2) + pow((latitude - clat) * 110.57, 2))) AS gyration,
         avg((speed_kmh >= 5)::INTEGER) AS moving, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1
  FROM f JOIN c USING (bird)
  GROUP BY bird
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All birds' AS label, '$__all' AS bird, max(far) AS far, min(south) AS south, sum(km) AS km,
         sum(positions) AS positions, NULL::DOUBLE AS gyration, sum(moving * positions) / sum(positions) AS moving,
         min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1
  FROM b
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, bird, bird, far, south, km, positions, gyration, moving, t0, t1 FROM b
)
SELECT label                           AS "Bird",
       round(far)                      AS "Farthest, km",
       round(south, 1)                 AS "Southernmost, °N",
       round(km)                       AS "Km flown",
       round(gyration)                 AS "Gyration, km",
       moving                          AS "Moving",
       positions                       AS "Positions",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "First",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "Last",
       bird                            AS bird_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, far DESC

options.content:
### Lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge
Gulls GPS-tagged by [INBO](https://www.inbo.be/en) at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge, Belgium: up to 33 birds a year, a position every two hours, some wintering at home and some flying on to Iberia, Morocco or Mauritania. Every chart is one cross-filter, answered in your browser: **drag** across the timeline, the distance from the colony, the hours and months, the speed or the turning angle, or **draw an area** on the map, and the rest follows as you move. **Press play** to slide a window along the year. **Click a bird** in the table to follow it alone. *Gull year* picks the year.

FROM $gullSteps

options.content:
### Jaguars of the Neotropics
The [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2379): 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Sonora to Argentina between 1999 and 2016, most of them in Brazil's and Paraguay's Pantanal, where the map opens. **Drag** across the kilometres a day, the distance from each jaguar's range centre, the hours or the turning angle, or **draw an area** on the map: the map, the cards and the tables follow as you move. Pick countries in the timeline's pills; **click a study area** to fly there, or **a jaguar** to follow it alone.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per jaguar under every filter, the longest walkers first, under a row
-- for all of them, whose click lets the jaguars followed go.
WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM $jagSteps WHERE $__crossfilter($jagFilters)),
c AS (SELECT jaguar, avg(latitude) AS clat, avg(longitude) AS clon FROM f GROUP BY jaguar),
j AS (
  SELECT jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1,
         count(DISTINCT time::DATE) AS jdays, sum(km) AS km,
         sqrt(avg(pow((longitude - clon) * 111.32 * cos(radians(clat)), 2) + pow((latitude - clat) * 110.57, 2))) AS gyration,
         max(home_km) AS far
  FROM f JOIN c USING (jaguar)
  GROUP BY jaguar
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All jaguars' AS label, '$__all' AS jaguar, '' AS study, '' AS country, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1,
         sum(jdays) AS jdays, sum(km) AS km, NULL::DOUBLE AS gyration, max(far) AS far
  FROM j
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, jaguar, jaguar, study, country, t0, t1, jdays, km, gyration, far FROM j
)
SELECT label                              AS "Jaguar",
       study                              AS "Study area",
       country                            AS "Country",
       jdays                              AS "Days",
       round(km)                          AS "Km walked",
       round(km / jdays, 1)               AS "Km a day",
       round(gyration, 1)                 AS "Gyration, km",
       round(far, 1)                      AS "Farthest from centre, km",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last",
       jaguar                             AS jaguar_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: One row per jaguar under every filter, the longest walkers first. The radius of gyration is the typical distance from the jaguar's own centre, a measure of how much ground its range covers. Click a jaguar to follow it alone; All jaguars lets it go.
spec.title: Jaguars

spec.rawSql:
-- Every position, once: time, country, jaguar, km that day, distance from the
-- range centre, hour and turn are filtered in the map, on the GPU, where the
-- clauses of the jagFilters Mosaic selection land. Coloured by country.
SELECT jaguar AS trip_id, jaguar, study, country, time, latitude, longitude, day_km, home_km, hour, turn_deg
FROM $jagSteps
ORDER BY jaguar, time

-- One row per project under every filter, the largest first; a click flies the map to it.
SELECT study                                  AS "Study area",
       any_value(country)                     AS "Country",
       count(DISTINCT jaguar)                 AS "Jaguars",
       count(*)                               AS "Positions",
       min(year(time)) || '–' || max(year(time)) AS "Years",
       round(median(latitude), 4)             AS lat,
       round(median(longitude), 4)            AS lng
FROM $jagSteps
WHERE $__crossfilter($jagFilters)
GROUP BY study
ORDER BY "Positions" DESC

spec.rawSql:
-- Every daily position of the species picked, once: time, species, animal,
-- month, distance from tagging, km a day and turn are filtered in the map, on
-- the GPU, where the clauses of the oceanFilters Mosaic selection land.
SELECT tag AS trip_id, tag, species, time, latitude, longitude, month, from_tag_km, km_day, turn_deg, km
FROM $oceanSteps
ORDER BY tag, time

-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first: what there is to pick.
SELECT species                                  AS "Species",
       taxon                                    AS "Group",
       tags                                     AS "Animals",
       positions                                AS "Positions",
       first_year::INTEGER || '–' || last_year::INTEGER           AS "Years"
FROM $ocean_species
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per animal under every filter, the longest journeys first, under a row
-- for all of them, whose click lets the animals followed go.
WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM $oceanSteps WHERE $__crossfilter($oceanFilters)),
t AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1, count(*) AS positions,
         sum(km) AS km, max(from_tag_km) AS far, max(latitude) AS north, min(latitude) AS south,
         arg_min(latitude, time) AS lat0, arg_min(longitude, time) AS lon0,
         arg_max(latitude, time) AS lat1, arg_max(longitude, time) AS lon1
  FROM f
  GROUP BY tag
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All tags' AS label, '$__all' AS tag, '' AS species, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1,
         sum(positions) AS positions, sum(km) AS km, max(far) AS far, max(north) AS north, min(south) AS south,
         NULL::DOUBLE AS straight
  FROM t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, tag, tag, species, t0, t1, positions, km, far, north, south,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(lat1 - lat0) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(lat1)) * pow(sin(radians(lon1 - lon0) / 2), 2))) / nullif(km, 0)
  FROM t
)
SELECT label                              AS "Tag",
       species                            AS "Species",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First position",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last position",
       positions                          AS "Days",
       round(km)                          AS "Km travelled",
       round(far)                         AS "Farthest from tagging, km",
       round(straight, 2)                 AS "Straightness",
       round(north, 1) + 0.0              AS "Northernmost, °N",
       round(south, 1) + 0.0              AS "Southernmost, °N",
       tag                                AS tag_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: One row per animal under every filter, the longest journeys first. Straightness is the distance from the first position kept to the last, over the kilometres travelled between: near 1 a transit, near 0 a round trip or a stay. Click a tag to follow one animal; All tags lets it go.
spec.title: Tags

spec.description: Daily positions from 2002 to 2018, with every other filter as a pill. Drag across it to keep a period, or press play.
spec.title: Timeline

spec.description: The change of heading at each position, between the step in and the step out: 0° straight on, ±180° back the way it came. The tracks are smoothed, so turns are gentle: a narrow peak is a transit, the shoulders are foraging. Steps under 5 km have no heading and are left out. Drag across it to keep a range.
spec.title: Turning angle

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per year picked: the lesser black-backed
-- gulls INBO tags at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge (Belgium), from
-- the Zenodo copy of the Movebank study LBBG_ADULT (CC0), read through the
-- gateway's month-long cache. A year is up to 2 million GPS fixes, minutes
-- apart; the browser gets one position per bird every two hours, with the
-- fixes and the kilometres flown in those two hours, measured fix to fix.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual-local-identifier" AS bird, timestamp AS t,
         "location-lat" AS lat, "location-long" AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/zenodo/records/22083084/files/LBBG_ADULT-gps-${year:raw}.csv.gz')
  WHERE visible AND "location-lat" IS NOT NULL AND "location-long" IS NOT NULL
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY bird ORDER BY t)
),
slot AS (
  SELECT bird, min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon,
         count(*) AS fixes, coalesce(sum(km), 0) AS km
  FROM leg GROUP BY bird, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
),
-- The colony: the median of every bird's positions in June, mid-breeding.
colony AS (SELECT median(lat) AS clat, median(lon) AS clon FROM slot WHERE month(time) = 6)
SELECT bird, time,
       round(lat, 5) AS latitude, round(lon, 5) AS longitude,
       fixes, round(km, 3) AS km,
       round(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - clat) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(clat)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - clon) / 2), 2))), 1) AS colony_km
FROM slot CROSS JOIN colony
ORDER BY bird, time

spec.description: The gulls' positions as steps, built in the browser from the year read by the server.
spec.name: gullSteps

source.sql:
-- Each bird's two-hourly positions as steps, the measures of movement ecology:
-- the straight-line step from the last position and its speed, the turn
-- between the step in and the step out (0° straight on, ±180° back), and the
-- hour by the sun (UTC plus 4 minutes a degree of longitude).
WITH p AS (
  SELECT bird, time::TIMESTAMP AS time, latitude, longitude, fixes, km, colony_km,
         lag(latitude) OVER w AS lat0, lag(longitude) OVER w AS lon0, lag(time::TIMESTAMP) OVER w AS t0,
         lead(latitude) OVER w AS lat2, lead(longitude) OVER w AS lon2
  FROM $gulls
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY bird ORDER BY time)
),
s AS (
  SELECT *,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(latitude - lat0) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * pow(sin(radians(longitude - lon0) / 2), 2))) AS step_km,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(lat2 - latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * pow(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude) / 2), 2))) AS next_km,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(longitude - lon0)) * cos(radians(latitude)),
           cos(radians(lat0)) * sin(radians(latitude)) - sin(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(longitude - lon0)))) AS head_in,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)),
           cos(radians(latitude)) * sin(radians(lat2)) - sin(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * cos(radians(lon2 - longitude)))) AS head_out,
         epoch(time - t0) / 3600 AS dt_h
  FROM p
)
SELECT bird, time, latitude, longitude, fixes, km, colony_km,
       round(step_km, 3) AS step_km,
       CASE WHEN dt_h BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN round(step_km / dt_h, 2) END AS speed_kmh,
       CASE WHEN step_km >= 0.2 AND next_km >= 0.2 THEN round(((head_out - head_in + 540) % 360) - 180) END AS turn_deg,
       round(((hour(time) + minute(time) / 60 + longitude / 15) % 24 + 24) % 24, 2) % 24 AS sun_hour,
       month(time) AS month
FROM s

spec.sql: SELECT DISTINCT bird AS value FROM $gullSteps ORDER BY 1

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: the Jaguar Movement Database (Morato et al.
-- 2018, Ecology; CC0), 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Mexico to
-- Argentina, 1999 to 2016. Zenodo has it as a ZIP: GDAL reads the CSV inside
-- it by ranges of the gateway's month-long cached copy. Timestamps are local
-- and month/day/two-digit year. One position per jaguar every two hours, with
-- the fixes and the kilometres between fixes in those two hours, and the
-- kilometres of the whole day (day_km), which the dashboard filters days on.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual.local.identifier (ID)" AS jaguar,
         trim(regexp_replace("study.name", '^[Jj]aguar_', '')) AS study,
         country,
         strptime(timestamp, '%m/%d/%y %H:%M') AS t,
         "location.lat"::DOUBLE AS lat, "location.long"::DOUBLE AS lon
  FROM ST_Read('/vsizip//vsicurl/http://feeds/zenodo/records/5001568/files/DataS1.zip/DataS1/jaguar_movement_data.csv')
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY jaguar ORDER BY t)
),
slot AS (
  SELECT 'J' || lpad(jaguar, 3, '0') AS jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country,
         min(t) AS time, round(arg_min(lat, t), 5) AS latitude, round(arg_min(lon, t), 5) AS longitude,
         count(*) AS fixes, coalesce(sum(km), 0) AS km
  FROM leg
  GROUP BY jaguar, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
)
SELECT jaguar, study, country, time, latitude, longitude, fixes, round(km, 3) AS km,
       round(sum(km) OVER (PARTITION BY jaguar, time::DATE), 2) AS day_km
FROM slot
ORDER BY jaguar, time

spec.description: The jaguars' positions as steps, built in the browser from the database read by the server.
spec.name: jagSteps

source.sql:
-- Each jaguar's positions as steps: the straight-line step from the last
-- position and its speed, the turn between the step in and the step out (0°
-- straight on, ±180° back), the hour on the local clock the collars keep, and
-- the distance from the centre of the jaguar's range (the median of its
-- positions), which grows on an excursion or a dispersal.
WITH p AS (
  SELECT jaguar, study, country, time::TIMESTAMP AS time, latitude, longitude, fixes, km, day_km,
         lag(latitude) OVER w AS lat0, lag(longitude) OVER w AS lon0, lag(time::TIMESTAMP) OVER w AS t0,
         lead(latitude) OVER w AS lat2, lead(longitude) OVER w AS lon2,
         median(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY jaguar) AS clat, median(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY jaguar) AS clon
  FROM $jaguars
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY jaguar ORDER BY time)
),
s AS (
  SELECT *,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(latitude - lat0) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * pow(sin(radians(longitude - lon0) / 2), 2))) AS step_km,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(lat2 - latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * pow(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude) / 2), 2))) AS next_km,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(latitude - clat) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(clat)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * pow(sin(radians(longitude - clon) / 2), 2))) AS home_km,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(longitude - lon0)) * cos(radians(latitude)),
           cos(radians(lat0)) * sin(radians(latitude)) - sin(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(longitude - lon0)))) AS head_in,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)),
           cos(radians(latitude)) * sin(radians(lat2)) - sin(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * cos(radians(lon2 - longitude)))) AS head_out,
         epoch(time - t0) / 3600 AS dt_h
  FROM p
)
SELECT jaguar, study, country, time, latitude, longitude, fixes, km, day_km,
       round(step_km, 3) AS step_km,
       CASE WHEN dt_h BETWEEN 0.5 AND 6 THEN round(step_km / dt_h, 3) END AS speed_kmh,
       CASE WHEN step_km >= 0.1 AND next_km >= 0.1 THEN round(((head_out - head_in + 540) % 360) - 180) END AS turn_deg,
       round(home_km, 2) AS home_km,
       hour(time) + minute(time) / 60 AS hour
FROM s

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: what TOPP tagged, species by species, from the
-- same cached table as the tracks below.
SELECT species, taxon, count(DISTINCT tag) AS tags, count(*) AS positions,
       min(year(time)) AS first_year, max(year(time)) AS last_year
FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
              columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                         'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
GROUP BY species, taxon
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.description: The species on the Ocean predators tab, the most tagged first.
spec.label: Ocean species
spec.name: species

spec.sql:
-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first.
SELECT species FROM $ocean_species ORDER BY tags DESC

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per choice of species: Tagging of Pacific
-- Predators (TOPP), the Stanford Block Lab's satellite and archival tags,
-- 2002 to 2018, as the Animal Telemetry Network publishes it on ERDDAP: tracks
-- already smoothed by a state-space model, about one position a day. Read
-- through the gateway's month-long cache. One position per animal and day,
-- with the kilometres covered since the previous one. West of 100°E a
-- longitude moves 360° west, so a crossing of the date line stays one line on
-- a Pacific-centred map instead of a stroke across the whole world.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT tag, species, taxon, timezone('UTC', time) AS t, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
                columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                           'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
  WHERE species IN (${species:sqlstring}) AND lat IS NOT NULL AND lon IS NOT NULL
),
day AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, any_value(taxon) AS taxon,
         min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon
  FROM raw GROUP BY tag, t::DATE
)
SELECT tag::VARCHAR AS tag, species, taxon, time,
       round(lat, 4) AS latitude,
       round(CASE WHEN lon > 100 THEN lon - 360 ELSE lon END, 4) AS longitude,
       round(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))), 0), 2) AS km
FROM day
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY tag ORDER BY time)
ORDER BY tag, time

spec.description: The ocean tracks as daily steps, built in the browser from the species read by the server.
spec.name: oceanSteps

source.sql:
-- Each animal's daily positions as steps: the kilometres a day since the last
-- position, the turn between the step in and the step out (0° straight on,
-- ±180° back), the days since it was tagged and its distance from where it was
-- tagged, which traces a migration out and back.
WITH p AS (
  SELECT tag, species, taxon, time::TIMESTAMP AS time, latitude, longitude, km,
         lag(latitude) OVER w AS lat0, lag(longitude) OVER w AS lon0, lag(time::TIMESTAMP) OVER w AS t0,
         lead(latitude) OVER w AS lat2, lead(longitude) OVER w AS lon2,
         first_value(latitude) OVER w AS tlat, first_value(longitude) OVER w AS tlon,
         first_value(time::TIMESTAMP) OVER w AS tagged
  FROM $ocean
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY tag ORDER BY time)
),
s AS (
  SELECT *,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(lat2 - latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * pow(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude) / 2), 2))) AS next_km,
         2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(latitude - tlat) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(tlat)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * pow(sin(radians(longitude - tlon) / 2), 2))) AS from_tag_km,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(longitude - lon0)) * cos(radians(latitude)),
           cos(radians(lat0)) * sin(radians(latitude)) - sin(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(longitude - lon0)))) AS head_in,
         degrees(atan2(sin(radians(lon2 - longitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)),
           cos(radians(latitude)) * sin(radians(lat2)) - sin(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * cos(radians(lon2 - longitude)))) AS head_out,
         epoch(time - t0) / 86400 AS dt_d
  FROM p
)
SELECT tag, species, taxon, time, latitude, longitude, km,
       CASE WHEN dt_d BETWEEN 0.5 AND 3 THEN round(km / dt_d, 1) END AS km_day,
       CASE WHEN km >= 5 AND next_km >= 5 THEN round(((head_out - head_in + 540) % 360) - 180) END AS turn_deg,
       round(from_tag_km) AS from_tag_km,
       datediff('day', tagged, time) AS day,
       month(time) AS month
FROM s
